We further validated whether the difference exists for the CHGB48 SNP(rs236132) in previously collected 140 leprosy patients and 190 endemic healthy people. There was no significant difference for CHGB48 polymorphisms between the patients and the controls (Table 4). However, CHGB48 polymorphism in male population was found to be significant between leprosy patients and healthy controls. The distribution of GC genotype for male leprosy (50%) was higher than that of male control (39.4%)(OR = 2.85, P = 0.011). Meanwhile, the frequency of CC locus in male leprosy (16.3%) was lower than that of male controls (22.3%)(OR = 0.38, P = 0.03). These results indicated G allele of CHGB48 might be the susceptible site of leprosy for male population. The Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium test for all leprosy patients and healthy controls indicated the samples were representative of population.
